L379@P6: Immune-related endocrinopathies
L380@P6: Patients should be monitored for clinical signs and symptoms of endocrinopathies and for hyperglycaemia and changes in thyroid function (at the
L381@P6: start of treatment, periodically during treatment, and as indicated based on clinical evaluation). Patients may present with fatigue, headache,
L382@P6: mental status changes, abdominal pain, unusual bowel habits, and hypotension, or nonspecific symptoms which may resemble other causes such as
L383@P6: brain metastasis or underlying disease. Unless an alternate aetiology has been identified, signs or symptoms of endocrinopathies should be
L384@P6: considered immune-related

L418@P6: Immune-related skin adverse reactions
L419@P6: Rare cases of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), some of them with fatal outcome have been observed. If
L420@P6: symptoms or signs of SJS or TEN appear, treatment should be discontinued and the patient referred to a specialised unit for assessment and
L421@P6: treatment. Caution should be used when considering the use of treatment in a patient who has previously experienced a severe or life-threatening
L422@P6: skin adverse reaction on prior treatment with other immune-stimulatory anticancer agents

L444@P7: Immune-related myocarditis
L445@P7: Cases of myotoxicity (myositis, myocarditis, and rhabdomyolysis), some with fatal outcome, have been reported with nivolumab or nivolumab in
L446@P7: combination with ipilimumab. If a patient develops signs and symptoms of myotoxicity, close monitoring should be implemented, and the patient
L447@P7: referred to a specialist for assessment and treatment without delay. The diagnosis of myocarditis requires a high index of suspicion. Patients with
L448@P7: cardiac or cardio-pulmonary symptoms should be assessed for potential myocarditis.
L449@P7: Grade 2 myocarditis
L450@P7: Grade 3 or 4 myocarditis

L462@P7: Other immune-related adverse reactions
L463@P7: The following immune-related adverse reactions were reported in less than 1% of patients treated with nivolumab monotherapy or nivolumab in
L464@P7: combination with ipilimumab in clinical trials across doses and tumour types: pancreatitis, uveitis, demyelination, autoimmune neuropathy
L465@P7: (including facial and abducens nerve paresis), Guillain-Barré syndrome, myasthenia gravis, Myocarditis-Myositis Myasthenia Gravis Overlap
L466@P7: Syndrome, myasthenic syndrome, aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, gastritis, sarcoidosis, duodenitis, myositis, myocarditis, rhabdomyolysis, and
L467@P7: myelitis. Cases of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome, hypoparathyroidism, and cystitis noninfective have been reported post-marketing. For
L468@P7: suspected immune-related adverse reactions, adequate evaluation should be performed to confirm aetiology or exclude other causes

L573@P9: REGIMEN SPECIFIC COMPLICATIONS:
L574@P9: • Please refer to the relevant Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) for details.
L575@P9: • Cardiac and pulmonary adverse events including pulmonary embolism: Patients should be
L576@P9: monitored for cardiac and pulmonary adverse reactions continuously, as well as for clinical signs,
L577@P9: symptoms, and laboratory abnormalities indicative of electrolyte disturbances and dehydration
L578@P9: prior to and periodically during combination treatment. Nivolumab in combination with
L579@P9: ipilimumab should be discontinued for life-threatening or recurrent severe cardiac and pulmonary
L580@P9: adverse reactions.
L581@P9: • Immune and infusion related adverse reactions: Immune-related adverse reactions have occurred
L582@P9: at higher frequencies when nivolumab is administered in combination with ipilimumab compared
L583@P9: with nivolumab monotherapy. Please see Table 4 for dose modifications of nivolumab and
L584@P9: ipilimumab combination therapy or nivolumab monotherapy following combination treatment
